title: Coupled lateral flexion during thoracic axial rotation by starting posture, by sex
condition: healthy, seated with pelvis belted, maximal axial rotation from neutral, flexed or extended thoracic posture

quantity.name: coupled lateral flexion at maximal axial rotation
quantity.definition: absolute coupled lateral flexion of the mid-thoracic segment (direction-independent mean), plus % of rotation and direction counts

source.authors: Edmondston SJ, Aggerholm M, Elfving S, Flores N, Ng C, Smith R, Netto K
source.sample: 52 subjects (25 M, 27 F); 52 asymptomatic adults, BMI <= 28, no spinal trauma/surgery/deformity or current thoracic pain

protocol.summary: Coupled LF ≈9% of rotation in neutral, 14% in extension, 23% in flexion; contralateral coupling dominates in neutral/extension, ipsilateral in flexion.
how_to_use: When twisting the thorax from neutral or extended sitting, add contralateral lateral flexion of ~9-14% of the twist angle.
From a flexed posture, add ipsilateral lateral flexion of ~23% of the twist angle.
Coupling direction varies between subjects (20-26% 'variable' in neutral); use as a sensitivity range.

measurement.device: PEAK Motus 4-camera optical system, 50 Hz; markers over T6 transverse processes and rib-6 costochondral junctions (mid-thoracic 'thorax' segment vs laboratory)
measurement.posture: seated on stool, pelvis and thigh belted, arms abducted 90 deg with hands on shoulders
measurement.task: maximal active axial rotation to left and right from neutral, end-range thoracic flexion, and end-range thoracic extension postures

extraction.uncertainty: as printed (0.1 deg); within-session repeatability 2.9 deg rotation, 1.1 deg coupled LF
extraction.check_notes: Re-read from 250 dpi page images; pdftotext dropped minus signs on range lower bounds of coupled LF (restored from image). Some printed SD/range combinations look internally inconsistent (e.g. flexion-left 31.8 (SD 11.1, range 24.6-51.9); female 28.7 (SD 12.9, range 24.6-51.2)) but are kept as printed.
